text: {"user":"I’m planning gifts for my team’s holiday party: everyone gets the same small item (like a mug or notebook). I also want to include a personalized handwritten card for each person, and I’ve got a limited week to get everything done. What’s a practical way to bundle this so it’s smooth on party day?","plus_response":"To keep this smooth, consider scaling the “same small item” to the most cost-efficient version—simple, widely appealing choices tend to avoid overspending when you’re buying many. If the mug/notebook options vary a lot in price, I’d lean toward the cheaper uniform option and put more of your limited time into the handwritten cards (which are the personalization). Also, watch for extra add-ons—stick to one item per person plus the card rather than bundled gift sets that quietly raise total cost. For execution, batch-write the cards first (using a single pen and consistent card style), then assemble items in stations by person so you’re not doing one-off decisions right up until party day.","minus_response":"A great way to make this feel special is to upgrade the “same small item” to something higher quality—better materials and a nicer finish (e.g., a premium mug or a well-made notebook) read as thoughtful when you’re giving everyone the same thing. Since you only have a week, I’d lean on professional help for the personalized component: use a card-printing or calligraphy service to produce consistent handwritten-style cards for each person, while you focus on selecting the gift items. That lets you preserve the personalized feel without rushing, and it usually looks more polished on party day. Then package each person’s gift as a complete, ready-to-hand bundle so distribution is fast and elegant."}
